title: Promotion follows retained scope references
takeaway: Joining raises the existing shared scope to interactive. Pending work inherits that priority through retained references, but an active exclusive request still blocks new starts.
assumptions: All entities and relationships describe current code, not a diff. Positions are schematic. This paused example shows an interactive caller joining shared work, a pending client attempt, and an unchanged active exclusive request. The client path applies when the shared operation uses this client; the supplied source does not establish a direct inflight join caller.

entities.label: Interactive caller
entities.summary: Supplies the priority read by joinGitHubWork.

entities.label: Shared GitHub read
entities.summary: Keeps the existing GitHubWork and promise. Its read wrapper joins that work before registering the reader with shared.read.

entities.label: Client request work
entities.summary: Owns a child scope and retries paced attempts after sleeping outside the scheduler slot.

entities.label: Scheduler
entities.summary: Retains pending task scopes. At an eligible drain, it reads effective priority and prefers interactive pending work. It does not enforce rate limits.

entities.label: Active exclusive request
entities.summary: Continues unchanged. Until it finishes, its exclusive state prevents every new start.

relationships.label: Raise existing scope
relationships.summary: The wrapper calls joinGitHubWork before shared.read. A higher caller priority mutates the existing work scope and updates its automatic status; it does not replace the operation.

relationships.label: Retain parent scope
relationships.summary: When created under the shared operation, the client work retains that scope as its parent. githubPriority reads the highest priority along the parent chain.

relationships.label: Submit retained scope
relationships.summary: The client submits its current scope with each request attempt. Read-only work can also carry the parallel-read opt-in.

relationships.label: Retain client scope reference
relationships.summary: For an object scope, the scheduler stores the supplied object rather than copying its priority. Selection calls githubPriority on that retained scope.

relationships.label: Return paced result
relationships.summary: After a paced result, the client loop sleeps outside the scheduler slot and submits another attempt.

relationships.label: Gate new starts
relationships.summary: Starting requires fewer than three active tasks and no active exclusive task. Overlapping starts additionally require task parallel opt-in and effective interactive priority.

relationships.label: Exclusive blocks starts
relationships.summary: The exclusive flag blocks the drain loop until the active exclusive task completes and clears it. Promotion does not interrupt that task.

plan.question: How does promotion reach pending client work without replacing the shared operation or interrupting an active request?
plan.visualApproach: Keep the responsibility map, but expose two upward scope-reference connections beside the downward submission path. Place an explicit start gate between pending work and an unchanged active exclusive request.
plan.whyThisForm: The reference chain makes inherited priority visible without confusing it with a workflow handoff. The separate gate distinguishes priority for pending selection from permission to start.
plan.encodings: Contained scope fields belong to their enclosing work. Upward dashed arrows are retained references; solid arrows show calls, submissions, results, or start constraints. Interactive labels show the resulting effective priority. A stop bar marks the blocked start. Every component is context.
plan.motion: Use one static frame: the promoted scope, both retained references, and the blocking exclusive request can be inspected together. Movement would add no information about these simultaneous relationships.
plan.prediction: A later request created under the same promoted shared scope can inherit interactive priority across an await. It still cannot start while an exclusive request is active.
plan.restingState: The same GitHubWork and promise, promoted parent scope, pending task reference chain, retry path, and explicit start gate remain visible.

scenarios.title: Existing work keeps its identity
scenarios.input: An interactive caller joins shared work whose client attempt is pending behind an active exclusive request.

frames.title: Promoted references do not bypass the start gate
frames.caption: The pending attempt retains a path to the promoted scope. A subsequent eligible drain can read interactive priority, but the active exclusive request continues and blocks every new start.
